At core revision 50746174f97c068e31fbc70ae807d2efeb022fae, the official CPU image and wheel completed and the kernel suites produced: oneDNN 200 passed; attention 1206 passed and 1350 architecture-dependent skipped; activation 50 passed and 8 skipped; GDN 74 passed and 5 skipped. Its first SILU BF16 vec failure also repeated three times and once with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 with the same two elements, indexes, and maximum absolute difference 0.0015869140625 against atol 0.001, excluding random or thread-order fluctuation. A separate 96-shape diagnostic measured the error profile, and focused SILU/SWIGLUOAI comparisons showed that transcribing the kernel's fast-exp approximation into the reference did not eliminate failures; a sequential FP32 accumulation reference was element-for-element equal to the existing PyTorch reference in the audited failing shapes. These diagnostics exclude fast-exp alone and reference GEMM accumulation order as root causes, but do not establish a replacement accuracy contract. After refreshing origin/main to 5eca5cd55147f36e5951f3cb7992cd45356fda20, the branch has no diff from upstream in cpu_fused_moe.cpp, this test, or the default tolerance helper; only CPU dependency alignment differs among those audited paths. No kernel or tolerance was changed and this support gate remains failed as an upstream-baseline-equivalent issue, not an ecosystem-reorganization regression.

The failed official-cpu-kernel-ci validation records the executed subset and must be resolved independently before this broader validation can pass.

validations.evidence: Mooncake, LMCache, PegaFlow, and LMCache-Ascend systems/providers are separate from their connector bridges.

Core packages separate six-component Mooncake direct/store and LMCache v1/multiprocess bridge bundles with scheduler, worker, and API telemetry roles. Dedicated telemetry modules import no connector implementation. Five new bundle tests plus 67 affected typed-factory, config, Mooncake stats, and LMCache connector tests passed; all relevant core pre-commit hooks and the repository-profile schema passed.

At core revision 92f17aa124cd70ff9b0e919a856c0a41e062cc27, seven focused tests verify that Mooncake direct/store and LMCache v1/multiprocess typed scheduler and worker roles resolve to the exact legacy implementation class, legacy next-start rollback names resolve back to that class, loadable telemetry codecs preserve stats type and payload, and a missing optional lmcache dependency fails closed with the same ModuleNotFoundError root cause. The focused and affected typed-factory, config, bundle, and LMCache suites passed 64 tests with all pre-commit hooks; this does not claim real service or hardware equivalence.

Core revision 5734f0a4ea748d7b21464519a9b08081259b61a0 removes name-based pkill and whole-caller-process-group termination from the Mooncake disaggregated example. Prefill, decode, and proxy services run in separately retained child process groups; cleanup uses bounded TERM then KILL only for those groups. Two safety tests plus the seven built-in equivalence tests passed, bash syntax validation passed, and every available pre-commit hook passed; shellcheck was unavailable on host 112 and was the only skipped hook.

Core revision 01ddb821dca26a424da104af8fd46f9e7e80f71e provides topology-aware fail-closed preflight plus a direct-mode process-owned runner for mutually exclusive legacy, typed, and fresh-process rollback states. It checks exact source/CLI/runtime, roles, model, revision, GPUs/free memory, ports, and fresh evidence; repeats volatile gates; uses deterministic requests; detects child death; probes the proxy's actual OpenAPI readiness route; and maps HUP, INT, TERM, and USR1 to bounded cleanup of retained groups. Nineteen focused tests, relevant hooks, and external shellcheck passed. In one A100 window both real 7B prefiller and decoder reached healthy state, but no benchmark ran because the former harness expected a nonexistent proxy /health route. SSH interruption exposed the missing HUP path; the three exact process groups were subsequently terminated without touching other services, and both defects were fixed. A later audit briefly observed both 80 GiB A100s and required ports free, but an externally managed GLM-4 32B service automatically restarted roughly one minute later; final-revision preflight observed 9062 MiB free on each GPU and port 18000 occupied, correctly launched nothing, and touched no external process. Other connected GPU hosts do not provide the required two-device local topology. Host 112 remains dependency-blocked. No real-online, equivalence, hardware-performance, or Mooncake-failure result is claimed.

PegaFlow publishes split scheduler, worker, and API telemetry Bundle v1 components with explicit device, IPC, and egress permissions. Its lazy package facade preserves the legacy module export while API telemetry imports no worker facade. Typed and legacy config builders, manifest admission, safety logic, and connector regressions passed all 74 focused tests.

PegaFlow revision 9d7070d4202487848e1f65750699d0229c45619b vendors protoc for reproducible protobuf generation, builds the ARM Ascend server against the selected controlled Python, materializes that interpreter's virtual-environment and shared-library paths into the PyO3 server process, and makes exact Python ABI plus available torch.npu runtime explicit preflight gates. It retains exact core/provider source, runnable CLI, model, port, eight-device, manifest, unique-output, and owned-process-group checks. Five controlled-runtime tests, Python compilation, cargo fmt, pegaflow-proto tests, and the Ascend server build passed. A host-112 server smoke initialized ACL and detected Ascend runtime 1.17.0, then correctly failed before health because the controlled core environment is CUDA-only. A later read-only audit found all eight 910B2 devices idle with about 62 GiB free HBM each, but the CANN package set identifies as cann-9.0.0/26.0.rc1 and exposes HCCL v2 libraries without libhccl.so, while installed torch-npu 2.10.0 and 2.10.0.post2 binaries require libhccl.so. With CANN and Torch library paths configured, that is the sole unresolved extension dependency. The final typed preflight therefore correctly fails platform_npu_runtime. No connector, real-online, or hardware equivalence is claimed, and no ad-hoc compatibility symlink was created.

LMCache-Ascend publishes a wheel-carried split scheduler, worker, and lightweight API telemetry Bundle v1 manifest with explicit trusted-process permissions. Its dynamic adapter now accepts the host kv_cache_config constructor argument while remaining compatible with legacy two-argument callers. Six manifest, admission, packaging, constructor, and import-boundary tests passed with Ruff and format checks; the repository profile passed the closed organization schema.

LMCache-Ascend revision 754bbb0d3efcc876fbbe6f88100fa08a8c4252e1 binds its fail-closed preflight to the exact selected core and provider source trees, requires an engine-level vLLM import and runnable service CLI, tolerates runtime logs before the final JSON record, and retains the matched legacy/typed/fresh-process-rollback runbook. validations.evidence: External RIDE control plane, separately built remote runtime sidecar, and core-delivered local control host are three separate catalog components with independent topology, lifecycle, and authority.

Closed packaged action/receipt schemas, strict read-only health-probe parsing, and side-effect-free target, issuer-policy, scope, expiry, epoch, precondition, duplicate, and idempotency decisions remain covered.

Exact-wire-byte HMAC-SHA256 verification precedes strict parsing; a mode-0600 SQLite ledger binds idempotency key, action ID, and semantic fingerprint, restores in-progress actions and immutable correlated terminal receipts after restart, and rejects tampering, conflicts, nonterminal completion, and receipt identity mismatches. All 42 focused control-bridge tests and relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

A core-owned spawn worker materializes only for exact action/receipt v1, bridge-plane, process-isolated, IPC-only descriptors; it imports no bundle code and implements ready handshake, a single bounded request slot, timeout/failure cleanup, drain/stop, explicit restart, and runtime/epoch/state/receipt rechecks.

A transport-agnostic local service composes authentication, admission, durable lookup/reservation, and execution. Terminal retries after expiry restore the prior receipt; in-progress duplicates, semantic conflicts, executor failures, and unauthenticated inputs remain non-mutating and do not re-execute. All 24 affected security/service tests and relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

The host adapter reuses EngineClient.check_health, distinguishes healthy, EngineDeadError, and unavailable outcomes, strips exception detail, and passes only a closed source/timestamp/state observation to the child. Future or older-than-five-second observations fail closed, and missing observations remain RUNTIME_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE. All 23 affected health, executor, and service tests plus relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

Canonical v1 signatures select exact issuer/key IDs from immutable monotonic generations with activation, expiry, revocation, overlap, atomic replacement, and rollback prevention. Versioned mode rejects unknown IDs and legacy downgrade; explicit legacy mappings remain compatible. The same action re-signed by a new key restores its terminal receipt after the old key is removed without re-execution. All 32 affected key, security, and service tests plus relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

A Linux same-UID Unix-domain-socket host uses SO_PEERCRED, mode-0600 sockets, secure pre-existing parent ownership, exact bounded frames, HMAC message authentication, bounded concurrent ingress, one serialized authority lane, generic error envelopes, timeout-to-pending recovery, and inode-safe cleanup. A timed-out operation retains its slot until durable completion, preventing an unbounded executor queue. All 31 affected transport, security, and service tests plus relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

The OpenAI server accepts an absolute --control-bridge-config only when explicitly supplied. Its closed v1 configuration references separate host-owned mode-private base64 key files, grants exactly runtime.read, bounds all limits, rejects multi-API-process ambiguity, and lets FastAPI lifespan own startup and reverse-order cleanup of the fixed executor, ledger, service, health adapter, and socket. All 51 combined control-bridge tests and 38 existing CLI/server-lifecycle tests passed with relevant pre-commit hooks.

A separately built pure-Python sidecar terminates TLS 1.3 with mandatory client certificates, enforces an exact certificate SHA-256 allowlist, preserves bounded VLCB1 frames, and forwards them to the same-UID local host without parsing actions or importing vLLM. Seven tests include a real ephemeral-CA mTLS-to-UDS round trip; Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, markdown, and relevant pre-commit hooks passed.

The fixed read-only action is now runnable through an experimental local mTLS-to-UDS path. Production certificate issuance/rotation/revocation, secret backend and audit integration, high availability/reconnect policy, a general or mutating runtime operation API, and OS capability confinement for non-core code remain absent.

blockers: Only the read-only health-probe contract is defined; no general or mutating runtime action exists.

The experimental sidecar provides TLS 1.3 mutual authentication and certificate-fingerprint admission, but production certificate issuance, rotation, revocation, secret distribution, audit, high availability, and reconnect policy remain undefined.
The fixed core worker and local socket do not provide OS capability confinement for future non-core bridge code.

Generic Bundle v1 startup still rejects process isolation. Non-empty permissions require an explicit host allowlist but remain admission metadata rather than OS confinement; the explicit local host can materialize only the fixed core health-probe descriptor and cannot run bundle-supplied bridge code.
rollback: Keep the bridge unconfigured; default runtime behavior remains independent of the external control plane.

known_limitations: The documentation repository revision records the parent snapshot because a release record cannot contain the hash of the commit that contains itself; the published branch head is the authoritative record revision.
All listed writable branches exist on GitHub, but no pull request is merged and no registry tag is published.
The legacy vllm-ascend-hust-bidkv repository is GitHub-archived and rejects branch writes; its immutable main revision is classified centrally, while new BidKV integration belongs to vllm-hust-bidkv.

BidKV legacy/typed equivalence is proven for a versioned deterministic scheduler contract trace, metrics, snapshots, initialization failure, and next-start rollback; no real online workload, accelerator behavior, or performance equivalence is inferred from that replay.
One MultiConnector consistency test requires authenticated access to the gated meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct model and was not run.
Typed single and ordered_multi KV materialization are experimental; real-system equivalence is not claimed, and the local same-UID control transport is not a production remote RIDE bridge.

The official CPU image is reproducible and ABI-aligned, but its fused-MoE BF16 vec matrix currently has 17 reproducible numerical failures out of 96 cases. The audited implementation, test, and tolerance files are identical to upstream main, and focused diagnostics exclude fast-exp alone and reference accumulation order as sufficient causes. This does not block publishing the opt-in ecosystem reorganization with experimental labels, but no supported or candidate label may rely on the CPU gate until the upstream kernel/reference contract is resolved and rerun.

No completed serving request or benchmark was executed on NPU, GPU, or Apple Silicon for this draft. Accelerator startup evidence is limited to healthy real-model Mooncake prefiller/decoder processes before the corrected matrix, plus PegaFlow ACL/runtime initialization before its torch_npu gate failed; neither is connector-equivalence or performance evidence.
This draft authorizes no legacy entry-point deprecation or removal.
